scope: Step 6 moves every generated slot body and every chain-owned hand body to the port class of its retail owner: the entity chain's bodies onto FElysiumEntity, FElysiumAnimating, the new FElysiumAnimatingOverlay and FElysiumFlex, and FElysiumCombatCharacter; the NPC layers' stay on FElysiumNpcBase / FElysiumNpc. Stubs keep counting and name their retail owner; one dead stub is deleted; the eight entity-method candidates get their audited dispositions; obsolete tables whose last consumer is a test are retired; kernel_shape --unported pins the live unported rule set; the census tests check owners. The ten deferred classes stay listed.

owner_decisions.2026-09-26 chain classes: Add FElysiumAnimatingOverlay (CBaseAnimatingOverlay) and FElysiumFlex (CBaseFlex) between FElysiumAnimating and FElysiumCombatCharacter, each with its own cpp; register their abstract descriptors. Their datamaps name no external, so they get no binding class. They are declared in ElysiumPlayer.h between the two classes they sit between, where the chain's other two nodes already are: FElysiumCombatCharacter needs them complete, so a header of their own would have to be included mid-file.
owner_decisions.2026-09-26 stub text: A generated stub's surface names its retail owner (CBaseEntity::X, CBaseFlex::X, CAI_BaseNPC::X, CAI_BaseNPCTroika::X) instead of CAI_BaseNPCTroika::X for every row. Each changed observed message is a diagnostic_remap expectation; test_delta refuses a remap that changes the address or the receiver.
owner_decisions.2026-09-26 stub deletion: Delete only a stub with a `dead` verdict, no C++ caller and no override in any class. Every other stub stays with a recorded disposition; no reachability study in this step.
owner_decisions.2026-09-26 commit split: 6a (records and checker, no C++) and 6b (the two chain classes, full gate) are their own commits; 6c-6i land as the one step-6 commit.

rules.owner: A body's owner is the most-base class of the retail chain CBaseEntity -> CBaseToggle -> CBaseAnimating -> CBaseAnimatingOverlay -> CBaseFlex -> CBaseCombatCharacter -> CAI_BaseNPC -> CAI_BaseNPCTroika whose primary vtable holds the same (thunk-resolved) pointer at that slot. Ghidra's namespace label is not an owner (95 CBaseEntity-held bodies are labelled CAISound::).
rules.declaration: A slot's virtual is declared on the port class of its introducer (the most-base table that holds the slot) with that class's own body; every more-derived chain class whose table changes the pointer overrides it. No introducer body in this chain is _purecall or missing.
rules.toggle: The port has no CBaseToggle node (gen_kernel_bindings' stated divergence). CBaseToggle's own bodies (slots 5, 31, 82, 108-110, 133, 135, 152) go on FElysiumAnimating, the nearest port class below it; where CBaseAnimating refills the slot, its body wins there.
rules.new_chain_rows: 102 rows are chain classes' own bodies the NPC does not run (an introducer or intermediate body under a more-derived owner). They are emitted as stubs of that body on its class, never as behaviour. Nothing calls them on a non-NPC receiver today; a stub fired on a new receiver class is a behaviour delta that test_delta reports.
rules.hand_closure: A chain-owned hand body moves with the members it reaches (moves-step6.tsv): a member follows its most-base user. A member that stands for an NPC-layer word (the shape map's CAI_BaseNPC band) blocks the move; a carrier that stands for a chain word moves up with its word. A retail chain body's +0x98 m_pBaseNPCTroika arm stays an AsNpc() arm (FireBullets 185, FInAimCone 364/365), never a cast.
rules.requalify: A qualified direct call FElysiumNpcBase::X to a body that moves is requalified to its new owner.
rules.save_order: Moved words keep their existing Serialize lines (the NPC base still writes them); save files are disposable (CLAUDE.md).
rules.name_hazard: FElysiumNpcBase is a prefix of FElysiumNpcBaseBoss, FElysiumAnimating a prefix of FElysiumAnimatingOverlay: every codemod and checker match uses word boundaries.
rules.collisions: gen_kernel_shape's reserved-name scan covers every class that derives from the chain across Source/ (the player, items, props, makers, directors and the rest of the ~50 FElysiumEntity subclasses): a same-name member there fails generation until SLOT_PORT_MAP resolves it.

findings.finding: None of AcceptInput, GetAbsOrigin, GetAngles, GetModelIndex, GetOrigin, SetMoveType, SetOrigin and Weapon_Switch is declared on FElysiumEntity/FElysiumAnimating/FElysiumCombatCharacter (gen_kernel_shape's reserved-name scan would have refused the clash). The overlap is the Origin/Angles fields, SetRuntimeOrigin, FElysiumEntityWorld::AcceptInput and FElysiumInventory::SetActiveWeapon. spec.md's 'merge into that method' is corrected to the audited dispositions (integrations below).

CBaseCombatCharacter::Weapon_Switch 0x1032dde0 gates on Weapon_CanSwitchTo, returns true early when the weapon is already the active weapon or armour, has an armour branch (m_hActiveIArmor/m_hLastIArmor), records m_hLastWeapon/m_hLastMeleeWeapon, lets the outgoing weapon refuse through its slot +0x4f0, then deploys (+0x4ec) and wields. FElysiumInventory::SetActiveWeapon ports only the swap. An adapter would publish a partial body under the retail name, so slot 388 stays a counting stub on FElysiumCombatCharacter; its callers (Ming Xiao, Bach) are unported species rules.

CBaseEntity::SetOrigin 0x100b2be0 acts only when the new vector differs from m_vecOrigin (+0x41c): it invalidates (0x100b5340(this, 0x10800, 0), 0x100b52a0), copies, and sets +0x1b1. The adapter writes through SetRuntimeOrigin under the same difference test; the change-tracker byte stays the Slot88/89 refusal.

CBaseEntity::SetMoveType 0x100aad70 writes m_MoveType and m_MoveCollide only when the type differs, then notifies the physics object (its slot 25). The seam writes RetailMoveType/RetailMoveCollide under that test; the physics notify is a refusal (no IPhysicsObject).

The spec's '38 linker-folded bodies' are the 38 CAISound-labelled default bodies of the pre-split surface that CBaseEntity introduces and holds (slots 32, 33, 36, 40, 41, 43, 44, 46, 47, 101, 112, 115, 131, 132, 139, 147-151, 156, 157, 162, 169, 170, 179, 182, 183, 186-188, 190, 191, 205, 206, 224, 235, 236); all go on FElysiumEntity.

The generated-body headline is 269 (83 defaults + 186 stubs), not 268/82: one default. Packet 5e-5f's '248 stub / 177 hand' base counts are stale; the committed ElysiumNpcBaseSlots.cpp says 233 stub / 192 hand / 127 default.

Of the 552 base rows, 347 are chain-owned (CBaseEntity 178, CBaseToggle/CBaseAnimating 25, CBaseAnimatingOverlay 14, CBaseFlex 15, CBaseCombatCharacter 115): 191 stubs, 72 defaults, 84 hand bodies. 205 stay on FElysiumNpcBase; the 170 Troika rows stay on FElysiumNpc.

Step 5 moved ScheduleHost.AttackExtentsCm (+0x50 CBaseEntity m_vecAttackExtents) to the base host; its reader GetAttackExtents 0x1009b030 and writer SetAttackExtents 0x1009af40 (slot 15, SLOT_PORT_MAP FElysiumNpc::SetAttackExtents) are CBaseEntity bodies. The word and both bodies move to FElysiumEntity.

FElysiumNpcBase::NpcFlags stands for m_bfAINPCFlags/m_bfAINPCFlags2 (+0x14b8/+0x14bc), which the census lays out on CBaseCombatCharacter; CanBeFedUponBy 0x10339800 (CBaseCombatCharacter) reads flags2. NpcFlags follows its most-base user to FElysiumCombatCharacter.

12 base stub rows carry a dead verdict. 11 are overridden (TraceMessage/TraceMessageBare 17-20 and GetLastThink 412-415 by Troika hand bodies; StartTask/RunTask 441/443 and GetSchedulingErrorName 451 by Troika). Only ReportOverThinkLimit 582 has no caller and no override.
